payload.claim: The predecessor task is first identified correctly by matching `pushed_sha == tree_base` on line 965-969 (`parent`), but its branch is then looked up by discarding that specific task and instead taking `_newest_for_spec(...)`, i.e. whichever task is newest for that spec_id, regardless of whether it is the same task as `parent`. `tasks_by_spec_id`'s own docstring (saffron/ledger.py:1097-1101) confirms a spec_id can carry several tasks across states (e.g. a later re-run or an ORPHANED retry) with different branches. If the task that actually pushed `tree_base` is not the newest task of its spec, `parent_branch` silently names the wrong, unrelated task's branch instead of the one `tree_base` was cut from. The shipped tests only ever create one task per parent spec_id, so this divergence between 'the task that pushed this sha' and 'the newest task of that spec' never gets exercised.
